checks: The convex norm inequality gives exactly three concentric integer disks of radii 1,2,1. At a nonnegative threshold s the endpoint sum is even in the tilt and is nondecreasing for nonnegative tilt, since |s−v|≤|s+v| and the chord profile decreases in absolute height. Saturated thresholds are included by extending the chord profile by zero.

For s≤0, comparing s+v with −s+v and using disk symmetry gives endpoint sum at least π. The middle area is at least 2π. At any nonvertical direction through y_t one has s∈[−t,t]. The nonnegative-threshold minimum decreases strictly up to t, and V(t)<3π. A through-mark vertical cap takes at least the middle and one endpoint disk, totaling 5π.

All three chords are proper at the horizontal level 0<t<1. Their common continuous midpoint is (0,t) and the equal endpoint weights cancel the integer coordinate. This is the full actual section centroid.

Direct differentiation gives the stated V′ and V″, with V′ bounded, V(1−)>0, and the endpoint-disk part of V″ tending to positive infinity. The second-derivative formula for a fixed p>0 is therefore positive for all sufficiently large t<1.

The original §3 uses the same all-normal proof and exact formula. A separate same-wave source concerning the identical body's section-length profile does not prove the assertion about positive powers of the optimized cap volume.
readability: The optimized scalar V is raw cap area; its derivative is the negative of the section-length profile. These quantities have distinct concavity assertions.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The horizontal cap is globally minimal at every prescribed mark. Its optimized area has divergent positive second derivative near the endpoint, which defeats every fixed positive concave power.
